a_guis.question: Is spearfishing (spear guns, pole spears, Hawaiian slings, other projectile devices) still prohibited in all Gulf Islands National Seashore waters under the current Superintendent's Compendium, and what is the Seashore's offshore water boundary?
a_guis.checked: 30 Sep 2026, Chrome (desktop), all accordion bodies of the compendium page present in the DOM (151,606 characters of text) searched for spear, projectile, Hawaiian, sling, harpoon, gig, bow and, arrow.

current_compendium.result: NOT FOUND. The current web compendium contains no spear, speargun, pole spear, Hawaiian sling or projectile-device provision. The only hit for 'arrow' is inside the word 'wheelbarrows'. The two fishing sections read as follows.
current_compendium.section_1_5_a_1_fishing_closures_verbati: a. Fishing and cast netting from public boat docks and boardwalks are not allowed in the following areas: 1. Fort Pickens and Ship Island ferry docks, 2. Davis Bayou boat ramp dock, 3. Ship Island cross island boardwalk, 4. In the small ponds and small creeks within the Davis Bayou area.
current_compendium.section_1_5_a_2_fishing_closures_verbati: The following areas are closed to fishing in accordance with the following conditions: a. Use of public fishing piers is restricted to the use of 2 forms of fishing devices per fisherman (i.e., 2 poles, 1 pole and 1 cast net, 1 cast net and 1 trap, etc.). b. Use of generators and the erecting of structures such as tents, canopies, tarps, or any other shelters larger than a beach umbrella is prohibited on public fishing piers. c. Public fishing piers are closed to the possession and consumption of alcoholic beverages and smoking products.

2021_news_release.verbatim: Fishing using bow and/or arrow, pole spears, spear guns, Hawaiian slings or any other projectile device is prohibited in all the waters of the Seashore.
2021_news_release.status: This wording is confirmed verbatim in the 2021 news release (the current guis-compendium url), but it is not in the current compendium.

florida.boundary_verbatim: In the Perdido Key, Fort Pickens, and Santa Rosa Areas the national seashore boundary extends on the north to the Gulf Intracoastal Waterway and on the south one mile from the low tide line of the island. At Naval Live Oaks the national seashore boundary extends 100 yards from the low tide line.

florida.other: All fishing regulations for national seashore waters in Florida correspond with Florida fishing regulations.

mississippi.spear_verbatim: For more information regarding spear fishing regulations, please consult the Mississippi Wildlife, Fisheries, and Parks website.

a_guis.reading: On the text the park now publishes, the Seashore-wide projectile-device fishing ban is absent from the current compendium (last updated 1 Sep 2026) and the Florida fishing page refers spearfishers to FWC rules. That points to the ban having been dropped, but an absence in a web page is not a rescission notice. Conservative reading for the map: keep the Seashore waters flagged (amber, 'ban published 2021, absent from current compendium, confirm with GUIS 850-934-2600') rather than drawing them open. Also note 36 C.F.R. 2.3(e) and any state rule still apply.
a_guis.open_question: Did GUIS formally rescind the 2021 projectile-device closure, or was it lost in the migration of the compendium to the accordion web format? Ask the park (850-934-2600) or request the signed compendium PDF.

b_marathon.finding: City of Marathon Code § 18-27 'Spearguns' bans using, firing or discharging a speargun on or below the surface of any manmade canal. Marathon is no longer on Municode: library.municode.com/fl/marathon now redirects to the city's own code site, marathon.municipalcodeonline.com.
b_marathon.location: Chapter 18 Offenses and Miscellaneous Provisions, Article 18-II Offenses Involving Public Safety, Division 18-II-1 Generally, Sec. 18-27
b_marathon.checked: 30 Sep 2026, Chrome; found with the site's own search box (term 'spear' returned one exact match, 'Sec 18-27 Spearguns'); rendered section text copied and re-matched string for string (all four paragraphs matched).
verbatim: Definition. A speargun is any device, whether commercially manufactured or handmade, which is so designed and constructed so as to be capable of forcefully discharging at great velocity any spear or any similar projectile in a direction determined by the user thereof for a distance greater than two (2) feet (24 inches), whether or not such spear or projectile is tethered to the firing apparatus or otherwise limited in its range. No distinction shall be made as to the mechanical construction or physical means utilized in such devices to create the potential energy necessary to eject or fire such spear or similar projectiles.
Prohibited activity. It is unlawful for any person to use, fire or discharge any speargun, as defined above, on or below the surface of any manmade canal.

Penalties. Any person convicted of a violation of this section shall be penalized in accordance with Section 1-7. In addition, any person convicted of a violation of this section shall forfeit the speargun used by such person in committing such offense to the City for destruction in the same manner as forfeited firearms are disposed of by the Sheriff.
b_marathon.reading: 'Any manmade canal' within the City of Marathon. No map of manmade canals is named in the section; the operative trigger is the canal being man-made. Conservative reading: every dredged canal inside the city limit is closed to speargun use, including residential finger canals and boat basins. This matches the flyer wording already in the registry (marathon-canal, keyssao.org) and gives it a primary source.
